articles.title: Your Canvas Is Freezing the Page. OffscreenCanvas Fixes That.
articles.excerpt: You open the profiler, record a session, and the flame chart looks great. 60 frames a second, steady, no dropped frames. You ship it. Then someone clicks a button while the animation is running, and f…
articles.body: You open the profiler, record a session, and the flame chart looks great. 60 frames a second, steady, no dropped frames. You ship it. Then someone clicks a button while the animation is running, and for half a second, nothing happens. Not a dropped frame — the whole page. The click just sits there, queued, waiting for a thread that's busy painting pixels nobody asked it to interrupt. Here's the part that doesn't show up in a frame-rate graph: your canvas animation was never competing with itself. It was competing with every click handler, every layout pass, every bit of input handling on the page — because by default, all of that runs on exactly one thread, and canvas drawing calls are first-class citizens on it. The fix everyone reaches for first The instinct is to blame the math.

articles.title: Next.js 16.4 ensureStatic: Locking Routes Fully Static
articles.excerpt: You ship a route you're sure is fully static. A teammate adds one fetch() call to a shared layout three weeks later — no cache directive, just a quick lookup they needed for a banner. Nothing errors.…
articles.body: You ship a route you're sure is fully static. A teammate adds one fetch() call to a shared layout three weeks later — no cache directive, just a quick lookup they needed for a banner. Nothing errors. The build succeeds. The route still "looks" static in dev. It isn't anymore: that one call now forces the whole subtree to render on every request, and nobody notices until the latency dashboard does. This is written against Next.js 16.4.3 (verified against the framework's own GitHub release notes and documentation as of October 2026). The guardrail for exactly this scenario — ensureStatic — was stabilized in 16.4.0 , after shipping unstable for a few releases.

articles.title: ElevenLabs vs four free voice clones: a blind test on my own voice

articles.body: I pay ElevenLabs $6 a month for a clone of my voice. Four free voice models say they are as good. So I made a clone of my own voice with each of them, hid which clip was which, and ranked them by ear. One clip in every round is the real me. The test One recording of me, made for this test, is the source of every clone. ElevenLabs' Instant clone takes 1 to 2 minutes of it; each free model took the length its maker's card asks for. Every model ran on its default settings and the first take is the clip. The free models are Chatterbox (Resemble AI), Qwen3-TTS (Alibaba), IndexTTS-2.5 (bilibili) and Fish S2 Pro (Fish Audio), run on one rented Runpod A40 each. Four rounds, six clips in each (five clones and the real me), shuffled by a script.

articles.title: PBO, Explained in Plain English: The Probability Your Best Backtest Is a Fluke
articles.excerpt: You tested 8 strategies and one looks brilliant. PBO asks the question most backtests never face: among everything you tried, how likely is the winner just the luckiest loser? You ran 8 versions of a…
articles.body: You tested 8 strategies and one looks brilliant. PBO asks the question most backtests never face: among everything you tried, how likely is the winner just the luckiest loser? You ran 8 versions of a strategy. Seven were mediocre. One was brilliant. You ship the brilliant one. Question: did you find an edge, or did you run a lottery and crown the winning ticket? That is exactly what PBO — the Probability of Backtest Overfitting — measures. And it is one of the least explained ideas in trading, because the people who understand it write papers, and the people who write blog posts mostly skip it. Here it is in plain English, with a worked example.

articles.body: 6 Min Read Happy 65 Years: NASA’s Johnson Space Center Then and Now View of the Manned Spacecraft Center during construction in 1963. Sixty-five years ago, a bold vision took root in Houston: a NASA center dedicated to human spaceflight. Since its founding, NASA’s Johnson Space Center has helped lead the nation’s human spaceflight program, supporting missions from Project Mercury through Artemis. Today, Johnson serves as NASA’s Center of Excellence for Human Spaceflight, and its workforce is helping to usher in a Golden Age of innovation and discovery. Johnson is home to America’s astronaut corps, the Mission Control Center, and the teams behind some of humanity’s greatest achievements in space.

articles.body: "Star Trek" celebrated its diamond anniversary last month, marking 60 years since it first aired on NBC on Sept. 8, 1966. There were a bunch of Trekkie-themed celebrations and news stories over September, including festive documentaries , special screenings , tributes, parade floats , interviews, and even a Galileo shuttle story. Now, publishers Penguin Random House and Ten Speed Press are releasing " Star Trek: The Original Voyages: A Visual History " on Nov. 10, 2026. This coffee table book promises unprecedented exploration of the pioneering space fantasy television series and enduring pop culture property that bolstered the space race and ignited sci-fi audiences' imaginations by taking us to strange new worlds and civilizations in the final frontier.
